---
title: "Effective context for CLAP and AST"
sidebar: cookbook
---

CLAP and AST return one native embedding per supplied audio segment. Their
processors have finite input capacities. Long waveforms now raise by default
instead of silently becoming a random CLAP crop or an AST prefix.

Provide explicit segments when every interval matters. To intentionally retain
one portion of a longer recording, choose a deterministic policy:

```python
from natural_features.features.audio.neural import audio_clap_embeddings

# Audio must already have the model's expected sample rate (48 kHz for CLAP).
features = audio_clap_embeddings(audio, context_policy="center_crop", padding="repeatpad")
print(features.time_bounds_s)  # Actual retained source interval
print(features.metadata["computation_context"])
```

`context_policy="error"` is the default; `"start_crop"` and `"center_crop"`
select a sample-aligned native-capacity window before processor normalization.
Returned timestamps and support refer to that window on the original clock.
The source-computation metadata retains the supplied interval, exact crop
sample indices, actual dependency interval, model capacity and padding policy.

CLAP capacity is read from its processor (commonly 10 seconds). Its explicit
padding options are `repeatpad`, `repeat` and `pad`; shorter inputs preserve
their original source support even when samples are repeated or zeros added.
AST capacity is derived from its native maximum spectrogram frame count and
25 ms / 10 ms frame geometry (commonly 10.255 seconds for 1024 frames). AST
zero-padding is recorded as `zero_fbank`. Unknown capacity is an error.

These policies do not provide long-recording pooling. Create and retain
separate segment embeddings, then apply any averaging as an explicit
downstream transform. Neither extractor resamples audio implicitly.
